ClinicalDocument.title: SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD — Frédéric Chopin Synthetic CCD

text.paragraph: Three months of cough, two weeks of blood-streaked sputum, night sweats, and weight loss: chest X-ray and CT, sputum samples, blood tests, home airborne isolation, and a report of suspected tuberculosis to the health department. Concerns: He has coughed for about three months, now with streaks of blood, sweats at night, and has lost weight; he wants to know what is wrong; He teaches piano at home and performs; he wants to know when he can teach again and whether his students are at risk; He is afraid his students and neighbors will shun him if they learn he may have tuberculosis. [S]

tr.td: Rifapentine 150 mg tablets, eight tablets (1200 mg) daily with food
1200 mg once daily with a meal by video-observed therapy with the health department, seven days a week, for 17 weeks (119 doses)
Moxifloxacin 400 mg tablet, one tablet daily
400 mg once daily with the other drugs by video-observed therapy with the health department, seven days a week, for 17 weeks; no mineral supplements within 4 hours before or 8 hours after
Isoniazid 300 mg tablet, one tablet daily
300 mg once daily by video-observed therapy with the health department, seven days a week, for 17 weeks
Pyrazinamide 500 mg tablets, two tablets (1000 mg) daily
1000 mg once daily by video-observed therapy with the health department, seven days a week, for the eight-week intensive phase (weight band 40 to under 55 kg)
Vitamin B6 (pyridoxine) 50 mg tablet, one tablet daily
Chest X-ray, two views: right upper lobe consolidation with a 2.5 cm thick-walled cavity and patchy opacities in the left upper zone; no effusion

CT of the chest without contrast: a 2.5 cm thick-walled cavity in the apical segment of the right upper lobe with surrounding consolidation and tree-in-bud nodules in both upper lobes; no bronchiectasis, no emphysema, no enlarged lymph nodes, no effusion
Chest X-ray, two views, at the end of treatment: cavity closed, with a small area of right upper lobe scarring; kept as the baseline for any future comparison

tr.td: Three months of cough, two weeks of blood-streaked sputum, night sweats, and weight loss: chest X-ray and CT, sputum samples, blood tests, home airborne isolation, and a report of suspected tuberculosis to the health department
Results visit: pulmonary tuberculosis confirmed; infectious diseases consultation and the start of the four-month rifapentine-moxifloxacin regimen by video-observed therapy
Two-and-a-half-week review: release from isolation, return to teaching, liver tests, and tests for cystic fibrosis and alpha-1 antitrypsin deficiency
End of the eight-week intensive phase: susceptibility results, the two-month sputum culture, and the start of the continuation phase
Same-day sick visit for a cold with cough during tuberculosis treatment

code.displayName: Periodic reevaluation and management of healthy individual

tr.td: Infectious diseases consultation to confirm the diagnosis, choose between the six-month and four-month regimens, plan monitoring and his return to teaching, and address cystic fibrosis and alpha-1 antitrypsin deficiency as explanations for his lifelong chest illness

Diagnosis: three sputum samples at least eight hours apart, one early in the morning, for acid-fast smear, nucleic acid amplification with rifampin resistance, culture, molecular testing for isoniazid and fluoroquinolone resistance, and phenotypic susceptibility; an interferon-gamma release assay; HIV, hepatitis B, and hepatitis C tests; and baseline blood count, liver and kidney tests, potassium, calcium, and magnesium

Infection control and public health: home airborne isolation with no students or visitors and a surgical mask around others; same-day report of suspected tuberculosis to the health department; a contact investigation of his students, friends, and other close contacts led by the health department
Nutrition: two dietitian visits in the first month, three meals and three energy-dense snacks a day, two oral nutrition supplement drinks a day, and weight at every visit

Support: plain information about how tuberculosis spreads, how quickly treatment makes him non-infectious, and that it is curable; help with what to tell his students; PHQ-9 at diagnosis, at two months, and at the end of treatment

Treatment: the four-month regimen of rifapentine 1200 mg, moxifloxacin 400 mg, isoniazid 300 mg, and pyrazinamide 1000 mg daily with food for eight weeks, then rifapentine, moxifloxacin, and isoniazid for nine weeks, with pyridoxine, by video-observed therapy seven days a week; complete when 119 doses are taken within five months

Monitoring: symptoms, weight, adverse effects (liver, tendons, nerves) and observed doses at every visit; liver tests at two to three weeks and for symptoms; sputum smears in the third week for release, then monthly culture until two are negative, including the two-month culture; phenotypic susceptibility including moxifloxacin; PHQ-9 at two months and at the end
Sweat chloride test and serum alpha-1 antitrypsin level once he is out of isolation, to address cystic fibrosis and alpha-1 antitrypsin deficiency as the proposed alternatives
Complete all 119 doses within five months by video-observed therapy
All 119 doses completed in 17 weeks: 56 in the intensive phase and 63 in the continuation phase, with none missed
Sputum culture negative at two months
The two-month culture showed no growth, as did the cultures from the third week
Return to teaching once the health department confirms he is no longer infectious
Released from isolation after three negative smears and more than two weeks of treatment; teaching again from the third week
Weight back to at least 55 kg by the end of treatment
55.0 kg at the end of treatment, from 48.5 kg at diagnosis
PHQ-9 below 5 by the end of treatment
PHQ-9 3 at the end of treatment, from 7 at diagnosis
